description: Like the C rule that whoever calls malloc frees, but checked: each value has one owner, and dropping the owner frees it.
The destructor that runs exactly once when the owner goes out of scope; it replaces free calls and goto cleanup chains.
A shared reference: like a const pointer that is never null and never dangles, and nothing mutates the value while it is in use.
An exclusive reference: what restrict promises, enforced by the compiler; no other access while it is in use.
A slice: a pointer and a length travelling together, with bounds-checked indexing.
A compile-time name for how long a pointee stays valid, the fact a C API documents in a comment.
Implicit bitwise duplication, like C struct assignment, allowed only for types that own no resources.
A tagged union whose tag and payload cannot disagree; match must handle every variant.
Replaces a NULL return: None is a separate value the caller must handle before using the payload.
Replaces -1 plus errno: the error travels in the return value and cannot be overwritten.
An owned, growable UTF-8 buffer with a stored length and no NUL terminator.
The unit of compilation: a whole tree of modules, not a single .c file.
The export marker; items are private to their module otherwise, the reverse of C's external linkage default.
A block where you, not the compiler, prove the invariants C always left to you.
Lays out a struct with C's field order and padding rules for the target.
A lock that owns the data it protects; the guard unlocks when it is dropped.
